newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia to boost efforts for Russia border deal.
newsitem.headline: Estonia to boost efforts for Russia border deal.

text.p: Estonia is to step up efforts to solve an unsolved border dispute with its huge neighbour Russia, a newspaper said on Thursday.

Eesti Paevaleht said Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi or Foreign Minister Siim Kallas would be named soon to try and solve one of the key questions for Estonia as it aims for European Union (EU) and NATO entry five years after regaining its independence from the former Soviet Union.

"It is one of the key questions if we want to get into the European Union and NATO as it is not good if we have an unsettled border question," Vaehi's spokeswoman told Reuters, confirming the newspaper report.

The two sides have settled the border line but are deadlocked over Russia's refusal to recognise a 1920 peace treaty between the first independent Estonian state and Russia, which had ruled its small neigbour for around 200 years.
Estonia says the treaty is still important as it was the only border treaty in force with Russia before Estonia was annexed by the Soviet Union in 1940.
It also has symbolic value as in the treaty, Russia promises to recognise "forever" Estonia's independence.
But Russia says the treaty is irrelevant to the current negotiations and ceased to become valid in 1940.
Estonia says it has already made a big concession by not making claims for the return of some 2,334 sq kms (875 sq miles) of land that belonged to the pre-1940 Estonian republic.
Russia says it has no border claims on its neighbours but will not entertain claims on its own territory either.
